title: Lark daily briefing — Fri 9 Oct 2026
summary: Two items today: a bootstrap result for inference after selecting a maximum, and an update to a recommendation world-model paper.

work.title: Bootstrap Inference for the Value of the Selected Arm

items.why_now: Gives a valid bootstrap for the winner's value under near-ties, which is the regime your ranking-uncertainty project struggles with.

contribution.question: How to construct confidence intervals for the mean of the empirically best arm.
contribution.obstacle: The max functional is non-differentiable at ties, so the standard bootstrap is inconsistent.
contribution.idea: Bootstrap a smoothed max with a data-dependent temperature that vanishes at a chosen rate.
contribution.main_result: Uniformly valid coverage over a class including exact ties, with interval length within a constant of the oracle.

claims.text: Coverage is uniformly valid over the parameter space, including exact ties.

evidence.quote: the proposed interval achieves uniform asymptotic coverage over Θ, including configurations with exact ties

claims.text: The authors suggest the method applies to adaptive experiments.

evidence.quote: we expect the approach to extend to adaptively collected data

connection.text: Could replace the conservative projection intervals in your winner's-curse correction; the i.i.d. condition rules out direct use with bandit-collected data.
